input: Buy and frame a vintage map for the study

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The subject of the map (world, country, city, historical region, celestial) completely changes where to look and what to buy.
Budget determines whether to pursue an authentic antique map, a high-quality reproduction, or a printed vintage-style map, and what framing tier is realistic.
The size of the wall space in the study dictates the map and frame dimensions, which affects sourcing and cost significantly.
Aesthetic style (worn/aged look, clean reproduction, specific era like 1700s vs 1900s) shapes which maps qualify and how the frame should be styled.
Knowing if this is a personal purchase, a gift, or a shared household decision affects urgency, approval steps, and personalisation needs.
Whether the user wants to source online, visit local antique shops, or use a print-on-demand service determines the entire shopping path and timeline.
Knowing whether framing is DIY, done by a professional framer, or bought ready-framed determines the scope of the task and what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Buy and frame a vintage map for the study
gold.taskDescription: Source and frame a vintage map to display in the user's study room.

questions.title: What geographic subject should the map depict?
questions.description: Establish the map's subject — e.g. world map, a specific country, a city, a historical trade route, or a celestial chart — to focus the search.

questions.title: What is your total budget for map and framing?
questions.description: Determine the combined spend the user is comfortable with, distinguishing between authentic antiques, quality reproductions, and budget prints.

questions.title: How much wall space is available in the study?
questions.description: Get the approximate dimensions or a sense of scale (small accent piece vs. large statement piece) to guide map and frame sizing.

questions.title: What visual era or aesthetic are you drawn to?
questions.description: Clarify stylistic preference — e.g. aged parchment 1600s cartography, clean 1900s colonial atlas style, or a specific colour palette — to narrow candidates.

questions.title: Is this for yourself or for someone else?
questions.description: Determine whether this is a personal décor choice, a gift, or a shared household decision, which affects personalisation and any approval steps.

questions.title: Where do you prefer to shop for the map?
questions.description: Identify the preferred sourcing route — online marketplaces, local antique dealers, specialist map shops, or print-on-demand services — to plan the next action.

questions.title: Will you frame it yourself or use a professional framer?
questions.description: Establish whether framing is DIY, outsourced to a frame shop, or bought as a ready-framed product, which defines the final steps of the task.
